haiku-low.q1: They see "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is sent and no record is created.
haiku-low.q2: They get the same generic reply, but no link is created and no email is sent. The limit is 3 per rolling hour.
haiku-low.q3: A link works for 30 minutes and only once. It ends sooner if it is used or superseded by a newer link.
haiku-low.q4: The link stays usable. The token is untouched, so the user can retry until it expires.
haiku-low.q5: None. All sessions, including this device, are deleted. The user is sent to the login page and must log in with the new password.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries 3 times, then logs the failure and drops the job. Nobody is told, so the user never gets the link and must re-request.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is put in the queued email job payload, and the worker sends it inside the link. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored.
haiku-low.q8: The server hashes the token with SHA-256 and looks up token_hash, requiring unconsumed status and expires_at later than now.
haiku-low.q9: It is the count of the account's password_reset_tokens rows with created_at in the last hour. Older rows fall out of the window by time; cleanup can delete rows older than a day.
haiku-low.q10: Every earlier unused link for that account is marked consumed, inside the same transaction, before the new link is inserted.
haiku-low.q11: The password hash update, session deletion and token consumption commit together. The confirmation email is queued after that commit.
haiku-low.q12: The conditional UPDATE ... WHERE consumed_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now() RETURNING user_id lets only one request get a row. The other gets zero rows and rolls back.

sonnet.q1: They see the generic reply "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is sent to them.
sonnet.q2: The reply is the same generic message, but no token is created and no email is sent (limit is 3 per rolling hour).
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes. It ends sooner if it is used (works once) or superseded by a newer link issued for the account.
sonnet.q4: Untouched and still usable. The form is redisplayed with the reason, and the user can retry until the link expires.
sonnet.q5: None. All the user's sessions are deleted (all devices, including the current one) and the session cookie is cleared. The user is redirected (302) to /login and must log in again with the new password; there is no auto login.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries up to 3 times with backoff, then logs the failure and drops the job. Nobody is notified, so the user is not told and never gets a link. They can re-request, and the new link supersedes the dead one.
sonnet.q7: The API generates the token (32 random bytes) and, after the commit, enqueues a "reset" job whose payload contains the link with the raw token. The worker sends it through the mail provider.
sonnet.q8: It computes h = sha256(T) and selects from password_reset_tokens where token_hash = h AND consumed_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now(). A row means the link is good. No row means invalid, expired, used or superseded.
sonnet.q9: It is not stored as a counter. It is the count of the account's password_reset_tokens rows with created_at within the last hour. Old requests drop out as their created_at passes the 1-hour window. Rows are not deleted on use, and cleanup may delete rows older than a day.
sonnet.q10: Within the step A transaction, after the rate-limit check passes (n < 3), all of the user's unused links are marked consumed (UPDATE SET consumed_at=now() WHERE user_id AND consumed_at IS NULL). This happens before inserting the new token row and committing.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: the token is burned (consumed_at set), the user's password_hash is updated, and all the user's sessions are deleted. The "password changed" email is enqueued after the COMMIT.
sonnet.q12: The conditional UPDATE ... SET consumed_at=now() WHERE token_hash=h AND consumed_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now() RETURNING user_id, inside the transaction, is atomic, so there is one winner. The loser gets 0 rows, rolls back and sees the "link has expired" page.
